messages:
maria (infra): Heads up — seeing interface flaps + RX errors on a subset of p8zn nodes in us-west-2, started ~08:12 UTC. East-west pod pings show 10-30% packet loss across the GPU cluster.

ajay (netops): Which nodes? any common kernel/firmware?

maria (infra): hostnames: gpu-usw2-3a-[12,19,21,23]. All started around same time. Quick ethtool stats from gpu-usw2-3a-19: 

```
# ethtool -S enp65s0f0 | egrep "rx_errors|tx_errors|rx_no_buffer"
rx_errors: 4,321
tx_errors: 0
rx_no_buffer: 0
```

maria (infra): dmesg has repeated `ENET_RX_FLOW_ERR` + firmware reset lines: `ena0: firmware reset 0x3` every ~30s.

taylor (sre): Are we using jumbo frames / MTU 9000? Any VXLAN/Geneve overlays in the path?

maria (infra): Yes, nodes have MTU 9000 on the host NICs, but vxlan interface inside the k8s overlay is 1450 for some namespaces. Suspect jumbo <> tunnel MTU mismatch. Quick `ip link` from same node: 

```
2: enp65s0f0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
5: vxlan0: mtu 1450 qdisc noop state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default
```

ajay (netops): Hm. We've seen older ENA firmware mis-handle fragmented RX descriptors when jumbo frames are present and there's an overlay encapsulation. Which ENA driver + fw are affected?

sam (oncall): Running `modinfo ena` and `ethtool -i` on two nodes: 

```
# ethtool -i enp65s0f0
driver: ena
version: 5.12.4
firmware-version: 2.3.1
```

and on good node: firmware-version: 2.1.0

ajay (netops): That matches a vendor bug we saw in their slack — firmware 2.3.1 resets RX path on fragmented jumbo+encap. If some nodes got staged fw 2.3.1 and others stayed 2.1.0, you'd get partial cluster degradation.

maria (infra): Rollout job did a partial push last night across us-west. Looks like 4/20 nodes got 2.3.1. The rest still at 2.1.0.

taylor (sre): Short term mitigation options: 1) disable jumbo frames (set MTU 1500 on host NICs and overlay) 2) pin ENA firmware back to 2.1.0 (rollback) 3) disable checksum offload / RX offload on NIC as temporary workaround. Any preference?

sam (oncall): Disabling jumbo frames is lowest risk and doesn't require vendor rollback, but will reduce throughput. We need to evaluate GPU job impact. What's expected capacity hit?

maria (infra): If we drop MTU to 1500 cluster-wide in the GPU subnet we'll likely see ~8-12% network throughput drop per host for RoCE-ish flows. That could increase training step times and cause some batch job backpressure. Estimate: 10% effective GPU capacity loss for high-throughput jobs while we keep jobs running.

ajay (netops): Rolling firmware rollback across hundreds of nodes is riskier (reboots) but will restore jumbo support. If we can tolerate the temporary capacity hit, do MTU rollback first to stabilize traffic, then schedule controlled firmware rollback during maintenance window.

nic-ops: I can script a targeted MTU change on the affected AZ (3a) first to limit blast radius. Plan: cordon + drain affected nodes in 5-min batches, change MTU host-level and overlay config, uncordon. Will tag GPU-ticket-427 for capacity owners.

maria (infra): I'll open the vendor ticket with logs + `dmesg` dump and ask about 2.3.1 hotfix. Also will revert the rollout job plan and mark firmware push paused.

vendor-bot: Created ticket VEND-1982 with priority P1: "ENA fw 2.3.1 RX resets with jumbo+overlay". Vendor assigned: netsw-fw-team.

taylor (sre): Action list: 
- [maria] pause firmware rollout + collect full node dumps (08:30 UTC)
- [nic-ops] perform targeted MTU mitigation on 3a (08:45 UTC)
- [ajay] prepare firmware rollback playbook (if vendor says rollback required)
- [sam] notify capacity owners + owners of prod jobs with high network throughput

sam (oncall): Heads-up email to infra-users@ with expected ~10% GPU capacity reduction in us-west-2 for ~2hrs during mitigation.

maria (infra): Doing the drains now on gpu-usw2-3a-12 then 19 etc. Will post updates.

ajay (netops): If anyone sees `firmware reset` continuing after MTU change, stop and hold — that indicates the driver is still tripping on other conditions.

maria (infra): First node MTU change done and uncordoned. Immediate drop in RX resets observed on that node (no more `firmware reset` in last 2 min). Running smoke tests for inter-pod traffic.

taylor (sre): Nice. Proceed with remaining nodes in the group. Keep update cadence every 10 min.

maria (infra): Continuing with nodes 19,21. So far so good, no regressions.

vendor-bot: VEND-1982 updated: vendor requests full `tcpdump -s0 -w` captures when issue recurs.

ajay (netops): Capture plan ready; will coordinate a filtered capture on affected hosts if vendor needs it.

sam (oncall): Closing the alert for now while mitigation proceeds. Reopen if packet loss >15% or pod restarts spike.

maria (infra): Post-mortem/ops note to follow once we finish rollback or vendor confirms fix.
